Blockchain and IoT: All the important knowledge for Tech Leaders

AuthorPhuong Ly
Year2026

Scope of Work

Development method

Table of contents

The number of connected devices is growing rapidly globally. According to forecasts, by the end of 2024, the total number of connected IoT devices will reach about 18.8 billion, an increase of 13% compared to the previous year. This increase demonstrates the increasingly important role of the Internet of Things (IoT) in many industries. Notably, the link between blockchain andIoTis becoming a prominent trend.

At the same time, blockchain technology is also developing strongly. According to a research report, the global blockchain market size is forecast to increase from 7.4 billion USD in 2022 to 94.5 billion USD in 2027, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 66.2%. This reflects the increasingly profound application of blockchain in practice.

However, integrating these two technologies still has many challenges. One of the big issues is scalability, as blockchain networks need to process huge volumes of data from IoT devices. To solve it, solutions such as new consensus mechanisms and Layer 2 technology are being developed. Besides, interoperability between different blockchain networks also poses security risks, requiring businesses to have effective data and asset protection strategies.

For technology leaders, understanding and taking ownershipintegration between blockchain and IoTis the key factor. When deployed properly, this combination not only enhances security but also improves operational efficiency and opens up new business models. In the context of strong digital transformation, knowledge of these two technologies will be an important competitive advantage for businesses.

How Blockchain Enhances IoT Systems

The combination of IoT andblockchainis changing the way devices communicate and secure data. When the number of connected IoT devices is forecast to reach18.8 billionAs the year ends, ensuring the data generated by these devices is protected and intact becomes an urgent requirement.

Secure communication between devices (Device-to-Device)

One of the biggest challenges of the rapidly growing IoT ecosystem is ensuring secure communication between devices. With tens of billions of connected devices, maintaining a reliable data transmission environment is vital. This is where the combination of blockchain and IoT is clearly effective.

Blockchain provides a distributed and immutable ledger that records all transactions between IoT devices. As a result, the data exchanged becomes transparent, verifiable and nearly impossible to edit, thereby minimizing the risk of unauthorized access or data leakage.

In smart home systems, blockchain can ensure communication between devices such as door locks, air conditioners, cameras... is always safe, prevents unauthorized control actions and protects user privacy.

In addition, blockchain's decentralization helps eliminate "single point of failure", increasing resilience to cyber attacks. Consensus mechanisms also ensure that only valid data is written to the system, maintaining data integrity across the network. This is especially important in areas such as supply chains, where it is necessary to continuously track the origin and status of goods in real time.

Create an uneditable audit trail (Tamper-proof Audit Trail)

Another important benefit of integrating blockchain into IoT is the ability to create data records that cannot be altered. This helps ensure data transparency and reliability throughout the system.

In supply chain management, this combination enables real-time tracking of goods. IoT sensors collect data about conditions such as temperature, humidity... and store it on the blockchain in an immutable form. Thanks to that, all shipping and transaction activities are clearly recorded, minimizing fraud and errors. For example, perishable products can be continuously monitored to ensure compliance with safety standards.

In the financial sector, blockchain combined with IoT helps improve the accuracy and security of transaction data. Financial institutions can use blockchain ledgers to reliably store transaction data, while also leveraging real-time data from IoT devices to more effectively manage assets and risk, as well as meet compliance requirements.

In healthcare, IoT devices such as health monitors can send patient data and store it on the blockchain. This data is only accessible by authorized parties, ensuring the privacy and accuracy of medical records.

Real-life example: IBM and Maersk in the logistics chain

Cooperation betweenIBM and MaerskThe TradeLens platform is a typical example of the application of blockchain and IoT in global logistics. Launched in 2018,TradeLensaims to digitize the shipping industry by providing real-time shipping data and documents, helping to increase transparency and efficiency in the supply chain.

The system uses IoT devices to collect data such as temperature, GPS location of goods and store it on blockchain. As a result, all stakeholders can access the same source of trusted data, reducing disputes and increasing trust. In its early stages, TradeLens recorded more than 154 million shipping events, with a growth rate of up to 1 million events per day, demonstrating the strong scalability of this model.

However, despite its solid technological foundation, TradeLens has not achieved widespread adoption across the industry. By the end of 2022, IBM and Maersk decided to stop the project due to lack of synchronized cooperation from parties in the global ecosystem, causing the platform to not achieve commercial effectiveness as expected.

Still, TradeLens is an important case study, showing both the potential and challenges of deploying blockchain and IoT in complex, multi-stakeholder environments. Lessons from this project continue to serve as a foundation for future supply chain digital transformation initiatives.

Typical applications of Blockchain and IoT in 2026

The convergence between blockchain and IoT is reshaping many industries through increased transparency, security, and operational efficiency. Forecast showsIoT blockchain marketcan reach about 1.2 billion USD in 2025 and increase to nearly 74.8 billion USD in 2034, with an impressive compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 58.21%.

Smart supply chain with real-time tracking

Supply chains are being strongly upgraded thanks to the combination of blockchain and IoT, allowing real-time tracking of goods with high transparency. IoT devices such as GPS and RFID sensors continuously collect data about location, temperature and condition of goods. This data is then recorded on the blockchain in an immutable form, making it easy for stakeholders to access and verify.

Thanks to that, businesses can accurately monitor the entire product journey, minimizing the risk of loss, damage or fraud. The trend of applying this technology is increasing rapidly, with the blockchain market in the supply chain forecast to grow at a CAGR of approx39,19%period 2024–2032.

Many large corporations such asHome Depotor Unilever has applied blockchain to improve the supplier dispute handling process and ensure ethical sourcing. At the same time, logistics companies like FedEx and DHL are deploying IoT-based shipment tracking systems that provide real-time data on the location, temperature and safety of goods. For example, the FedEx SenseAware® platform helps customers track sensitive shipments, ensuring product quality and integrity.

The combination of blockchain and IoT not only optimizes operations but also strengthens trust between businesses, partners and customers thanks to transparent, uneditable data. This will be a core factor to help businesses maintain competitive advantage in modern supply chains.

Energy grid with decentralized transactions

The energy industry is transforming with a decentralized power grid model, where blockchain and IoT play a key role in ensuring safe and transparent energy transactions. This model allows "prosumers" - people who both produce and consume electricity - to trade surplus electricity directly with each other, reducing dependence on centralized systems and increasing the resilience of the grid.

The blockchain market in the energy sector is growing rapidly, with a scale expected to reach3.1 billion USD by 2024and up to 90.8 billion USD in 2034, corresponding to a CAGR of about 41.6%. The growth of renewable energy and the need for efficient energy management are driving this trend.

IoT devices such as smart meters and sensors collect real-time data on power production and consumption. This data is recorded on the blockchain to ensure transparency and cannot be altered. In Germany, many platforms have implemented itPeer-to-peer electricity transactions(peer-to-peer), allowing households with solar power to sell excess electricity to neighbors.

In addition, utility companies are also exploiting blockchain and IoT to optimize grid operations. Thanks to smart contracts, energy transactions can be automated, reducing operating costs and improving efficiency. At the same time, this model supports the integration of distributed energy sources such as rooftop solar power and battery storage systems.

Medical monitoring with patient data integrity assurance

The healthcare industry is promoting blockchain and IoT applications to improve patient monitoring and ensure data integrity. It is expected that by 2025, smart wearable devices will account for a significant proportion of medical transactions supported by blockchain.

IoT devices such as health monitoring watches and biosensors can collect real-time patient data. When integrated with blockchain, this data will be stored securely, cannot be edited, and is only accessible to authorized parties.

Some typical models include:MedRec platformof MIT uses blockchain to manage electronic medical records, ensuring only authorized people can access them. Estonia is also a pioneer in applying blockchain to protect medical data and give control of information to patients.

Notably, more than 35% of health insurance companies are investing in blockchain solutions to protect and process data from wearable devices, while also preventing insurance fraud. This shows growing confidence in the ability of blockchain and IoT to protect sensitive data.

Combining blockchain and IoT helps healthcare organizations improve the quality of care, ensure data reliability, and build trust with patients through solid security systems.

Action steps for Tech Leaders

The convergence between blockchain and IoT is reshaping many industries, helping to increase transparency, security and operational efficiency. To take full advantage of the potential of these two technologies, technology leaders need to have a methodical and realistic implementation strategy.

Deploy small-scale testing (Pilot)

For businesses considering integrating blockchain and IoT, starting with small-scale pilot projects is the logical step. This approach helps evaluate feasibility, effectiveness and risks before expanding deployment throughout the system.

For example, in the field of logistics, a number of pilot projects have used IoT devices for asset tracking combined with blockchain to monitor the environmental conditions of perishable goods during transportation. Data such as temperature and location are recorded on the blockchain, ensuring transparency and traceability.

Similarly, in water resources management,test modelshas applied IoT to track water consumption and quality, while blockchain ensures the data cannot be altered. These experiments show the technology's great potential in solving resource management problems.

Starting from a pilot helps businesses understand the benefits and challenges, and collect real data to make appropriate expansion decisions.

Invest in personnel who understand both technologies

One of the key factors for successful implementation of blockchain and IoT is human resources. The demand for personnel with expertise in both of these fields is growing rapidly, while supply is limited, creating a large skills gap in the market.

To solve this problem, businesses can apply many strategies:

  • Upskilling the current team:Encourage employees to participate in training courses and certifications on blockchain and IoT to supplement skills and increase engagement.
  • Recruitmentstrategy:Look for candidates with relevant experience such as cybersecurity, data analysis, cloud computing - fields closely related to blockchain and IoT.
  • Cooperate with training institutions:Coordinate with universities and training centers to develop programs suitable to actual needs, ensuring quality human resources in the long term.

Investing in people not only helps businesses deploy technology effectively but also creates a foundation for innovation and sustainable growth.

Monitor and comply with international standards

To ensure that blockchain and IoT systems operate stably, securely, and scalable, tech leaders need to update and comply with relevant international standards.

Some important standards include:

  • ISO/IEC 30165:2021:Defines a framework for real-time IoT systems that ensures fast and reliable response in real-world scenarios.
  • ISO/IEC 17825:2024:Focus on security techniques for cryptographic modules, helping to detect and prevent non-intrusive attacks.
  • ISO/IEC 19790:2025 & ISO/IEC 24759:2025:Provides guidance on security requirements and testing methods for cryptographic modules, which play an important role in protecting data in blockchain and IoT systems.

Proactively monitoring and applying these standards not only helps businesses ensure compliance but also improves system reliability, interoperability and security.

By implementing controlled testing, making the right investments in human resources, and adhering to international standards, technology leaders can effectively leverage the power of blockchain and IoT, thereby driving innovation and maintaining a competitive advantage in the digital era.

Conclusion

The combination of blockchain and IoT is creating profound changes in many industries, especially in the aspects of data transparency, security and operational optimization. Forecast to 2025,IoT blockchain marketcan reach about 1.2 billion USD and continue to grow strongly with a CAGR of more than 59%, reaching nearly 74.8 billion USD by 2034.

The main driver of this growth comes from the increasing demand for secure and transparent data transactions. In the supply chain sector, businesses are leveraging blockchain and IoT to track goods in real time, ensure authenticity and reduce fraud. Meanwhile, in smart cities, these two technologies support effective energy management and improve public safety through real-time monitoring systems.

In that context, technology leaders need to proactively update trends and master key application models to exploit the full potential of blockchain and IoT. This will be an important foundation to help businesses promote innovation and maintain competitive advantage in the digital era.

FAQ

What is Blockchain and IoT?

Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that helps store data transparently and immutably. IoT (Internet of Things) is a network of devices that connect and exchange data. When combined, these two technologies help increase security and reliability of data systems.

Why should blockchain be combined with IoT?

This combination helps protect data from manipulation, increases transparency, reduces fraud risk, and eliminates a single point of failure in the system. At the same time, it improves operational efficiency and creates a foundation for new business models.

How does Blockchain help secure IoT?

Blockchain uses decentralization and encryption to record data. As a result, information from IoT devices cannot be altered and can only be accessed by authorized parties, helping to minimize the risk of cyber attacks.

What are the common applications of blockchain and IoT?

Typical applications include smart supply chains, decentralized power grids, smart healthcare, and smart cities. These sectors leverage real-time data and transparency to optimize operations.

What are the challenges when implementing blockchain and IoT?

Key challenges include scalability, implementation costs, lack of specialized human resources, and interoperability issues between different systems. Businesses need a clear strategy to overcome these barriers.

Where should businesses start implementing?

Businesses should start with small-scale pilot projects, then evaluate effectiveness before expanding. At the same time, it is necessary to invest in human resources and comply with international standards to ensure long-term success.

Dart is a general-purpose programming language developed by Google. This is an object-oriented language (OOP) and was intended to be an alternative to JavaScript. However, over time, Dart has become the core language of Flutter, playing an important role in building mobile applications. One of Dart's strengths is its support for asynchronous programming through concepts such as Future, async/await and Stream. Thanks to that, programmers can handle asynchronous tasks effectively, similar to the approach of ReactiveX (Rx) in reactive programming. The cool thing is that when you learn Dart, you don't just use it for Flutter. Dart can also be used to:

  • Constructionweb applicationswith AngularDart

  • Developmentbackend services

  • Create cross-platform systems

In the future, programmers absolutely canDevelop applications for multiple platforms with just one language: Dart.

Compiler: AOT and JIT

Flutter (Dart) uses a combination of two compilation mechanisms:JIT (Just-In-Time)andAOT (Ahead-Of-Time).

InDebug mode, Flutter usesJIT compilerto compile code at runtime. This makes it easy for programmers to:

  • Debug applications

  • Performance analysis

  • Use the featureHot Reloadto update the interface immediately

However, in this mode, application size and performance are not optimized.

InRelease mode, Flutter usesAOT compilerto compile the entire codebefore the application runs. Thanks to that, the application achieves:

  • Higher performance

  • Faster processing speed

  • Smoother user experience

Flutter's overall architecture

Flutter is made up of three main components:

  • Flutter Engine

  • Foundation Library

  • Widgets and Design Widgets

Flutter Enginemainly written inC++, is responsible for processinglow level renderingpassedSkia Graphics Libraryby Google. Engine also communicates with thePlatform SDKs like Android and iOS, allowing Flutter to interact directly with the operating system.

Foundation Librarywritten inDart, provides thebasic classes and APIsto build Flutter apps and connect to the Flutter engine.

The user interface in Flutter is built fromwidgets. Each widget representspart of the interface, from text and images to animation and layout. The special point isEvery UI element in Flutter is a widget, making interface building flexible and extensible.

Flutter also offers two popular design widget sets:

  • Material Design Widgets– according to Android design language

  • Cupertino Widgets– in iOS design style

Thanks to that, programmers can build experiential applicationsnative according to the standards of each operating system.

Platform Channel

Flutter provides the mechanismPlatform Channel, which allows Flutter appsCommunicate directly with native components of the operating systemlike:

  • Camera

  • Bluetooth

  • Background services

  • System APIs

In application architecture, Flutter can function asActivity in AndroidorAppDelegate in iOS. This means Flutter canIntegrate into existing native applications, or a Flutter app can also call native components when needed.

Thanks to this mechanism, Flutter deliversHigh flexibility in cross-platform application development, while still taking advantage of the power of native features on each operating system.

Flutter vs React Native vs Xamarin: How do they work?

How mobile application development frameworks work

To clearly understand the difference betweenFlutter, React Native and Xamarin, first we need to see how these frameworks work in the process of building mobile applications.

Native Development

In developmentnative, applications are written directly in the official languages and SDKs of each operating system.

  • Android: Java or Kotlin

  • iOS: Swiftor Objective-C

This approach deliversHigh performance and full access to system APIs, but the downside is that the programmer mustWrite separate code for each platform, which increases development costs and time.

WebView (First generation of cross-platform framework)

In the first generation of cross-platform frameworks, applications were built usingJavaScriptand HTML/CSSlike oneweb app.

Then this web application will bepackaged in WebViewto run inside the mobile application. However, this approach often encounters many problems such as:

  • Low performance

  • User experience is not smooth

  • Limited device API access

Therefore, WebView gradually becomes an ineffective solution for modern applications.

React Native

WithReact Native, the source code is written inJavaScriptand then communicate with native components throughJavaScript Bridge.

This mechanism allows React Native to:

  • Use native UI components

  • Reuse code between Android and iOS

However,JavaScript Bridgeis also a limitation because passing data back and forth between JavaScript and the native layer is possibleaffects performance, especially for applications that are complex or require high graphics processing.

Flutter

Flutter takes a completely different approach.

Flutterdirect compilation to ARM machine code (Ahead-of-Time compilation), meaning the application runs almostnativeon the device. Instead of depending on the operating system's UI components, FlutterBuild your own UI system using widgets.

This brings many benefits:

  • Very high performance

  • Consistent interface across all platforms

  • Powerful UI customization capabilities

In other words, Flutter almostHandles the entire interface rendering process yourself, instead of relying on Android or iOS UI systems.

One of Flutter's standout strengths is its capabilitiesBuild complex interfaces with high performance. Thanks to its own rendering mechanism, Flutter can help applications achieveSpeed up to 120 frames/second, providing a smoother experience than many other cross-platform frameworks.

Additionally, Google is famous for its constructionInstructions are clear and easy to understand, helps programmers access Flutter quickly and conveniently during the learning and application development process.

Instead of having torebuild the entire project every time a line of code is changed, programmers just need to save the file (Ctrl + S on Windows or Command + S on macOS) and the changes will be updated immediately on the application. This significantly shortens development and testing time.

Another advantage is that Flutter usesDart instead of JavaScript. With many programmers familiar with languagesstatic typingLike Java, Kotlin or C#, Dart feels more familiar and accessible than JavaScript - which isdynamic typingand sometimes makes it difficult for newcomers.

Disadvantages of Flutter

Although Flutter can achieve high performance on many devices, onlow profile or old devices, performance may not be truly optimal. In some cases, Flutter applications may not run smoothly on devices that have been used for many years.

In addition, even though Flutter has launched versionv1.0, this framework is still relatively new compared to many other technologies. Flutter is oneVery potential cross-platform application development frameworkand can absolutely become a game changer in the software development industry. If you are looking for a modern cross-platform solution for building mobile apps,Flutter is definitely worth a try.

Table of contents

Choosing a career path is just as important as choosing a major, because both shape your future in clear ways. For those pursuing the field of software engineering, you've probably wondered if this path is really right for you.

This question may be easier to answer when you are a student, but becomes much more important once you enter the industry. Taking the time to look back, evaluate yourself and determine a clear direction with specific goals will help you build a more oriented and sustainable career.

Instead of focusing on academic theory, this article provides a practical perspective on popular trends in the industry.software engineering, helps you understand your choices and plan your next steps.

Popular directions for Software Engineers when starting their career

In the early stages, software engineers have many career options. Some people love web development, others are passionate about mobile applications, games or more specialized fields. Each path has its own opportunities and challenges, depending on your interests and strengths.

Here are the popular directions:

Front-End Developer

Focus on building user interfaces for websites and web applications. Work is directly related to what users see and interact with, ensuring a smooth, intuitive and engaging experience.

Back-End Developer

Work on the server side, handle business logic, build APIs, manage databases and ensure the system operates stably and securely (for example, payments, user authentication).

Full-Stack Developer

Combine both front-end and back-end. Able to build the entire system from interface to processing logic and database.

Mobile Developer

Develop applications on mobile devices such as iOS and Android. Focus on optimizing performance and experience on many different types of devices.

Game Developer

Game design and development, including 2D/3D graphics, gameplay mechanics and interactive experiences.

Graphics Engineer

Work with graphics technology, creating high-quality images, animations or videos using tools like Unity or OpenGL.

DevOps Engineer

Connect development and operations, focusing on automation, system deployment, and ensuring a smooth CI/CD pipeline.

Security Engineer

Responsible for securing systems, data and applications from cybersecurity threats.

Data Engineer

Build and manage big data systems, support analysis and decision-making based on data.

SDET (Software Development Engineer in Testing)

Combine programming and testing, build an automated testing system to ensure software quality.

Embedded Systems Engineer

Software development for hardware devices (IoT, embedded devices), which require high performance, memory and stability.

👉 At this stage, testing many different directions will help you discover your strengths and interests, thereby choosing the right long-term path.

Software Engineer career development roadmap

Regardless of which direction you choose, most software engineers go through similar stages of development:

Junior Software Engineer

The stage begins with little practical experience. You will work under the guidance of a senior or tech lead, focusing on learning processes, writing standard code, and understanding how to operate real projects.

Senior Software Engineer (3–6 years)

After several years of experience, you reach senior level with strong technical skills, the ability to solve complex problems, and understand the entire software development lifecycle.

In addition, you also participate in mentoring, code review and contribute to system design.

Technical Lead (6–9 years)

Responsible for technical leadership on the project, making architectural decisions, coordinating across teams, and converting business requirements into technical solutions.

Team Manager

Focus on people management, team development, ensuring performance and aligning technical goals with business goals.

Engineering Manager (9–13 years)

Manage multiple teams or large projects, build development processes, ensure product quality and balance between technical and business strategy.

Principal Engineer (13+ years)

Senior technical expert, focused on systems architecture, long-term technology strategy, and complex problem solving.

CTO – Chief Technology Officer (16+ years)

Senior leadership position, responsible for driving technology, driving innovation and ensuring technology serves business goals.

Key Takeaways

  • Software Engineer has many different professional paths

  • Career paths usually start from Junior → Senior → Lead → Manager → CTO

  • Technical skills and soft skills are equally important

  • Determining direction early helps develop faster and more sustainably

Conclusion

FAQs

Which direction should a Software Engineer choose when starting out?

When starting out, you should try many fields such as front-end, back-end or mobile to discover your strengths and interests. Then, choose a suitable direction for in-depth development instead of scattered learning.

How long does it take to become a Senior Software Engineer?

Typically, you need about 3–6 years of experience to reach Senior level. However, time may vary depending on each person's ability, working environment and level of learning.

Should I pursue engineering or management in the IT industry?

If you love coding and solving technical problems, you should follow the expert direction (Senior, Principal Engineer). If you like leading teams and working with people, the management direction (Team Lead, Manager) will be more suitable.

Is Full-Stack Developer a good choice?

Full-stack is a good choice for people who want to understand the entire system and have the opportunity to be flexible in their work. However, to reach a high level, you should still specialize in one main area.

Does a Software Engineer need to learn more soft skills?

Yes. In addition to technical skills, skills such as communication, teamwork, logical thinking and problem solving are important factors to help you advance faster in your career.

How to develop quickly in the Software Engineering industry?

You should:

  • Do real projects regularly

  • Learn from senior code

  • Actively learn new technology

  • Practice systems thinking and problem solving

Should I change my career in Software Engineering?

Absolutely possible. The IT industry is very flexible, you can move from web to data, from dev to DevOps or AI if you have a good foundation and are willing to relearn.

Can a Software Engineer become a CTO?

Yes. Many CTOs start as developers. However, to achieve this position, you need additional management skills, strategic thinking and business understanding.

  • 9:00 AM – System check:Starting your day is not about jumping into coding right away. The first thing is to open the monitoring dashboards. I have to "check the pulse" to see if the "heart" of the SoftBuild system beat regularly last night, if the server is running stably or if there are any "red alerts". Only when the parameters display a safe green color can I really feel secure about taking my first sip of coffee.
  • 9:30 AM – Daily Stand-up:15 minute quick meeting with the whole team. Let's quickly update: What did we accomplish yesterday? Where to focus today? And most importantly, are you "stuck" at any step? At SoftBuild, we have the same unspoken rule:No one is left behind with a bug.Wherever there is difficulty, the whole team will gather to troubleshoot it.

Noon

Working process of a Backend Engineer

10:00 AM – 12:00 PM – Focused work time:This is the golden hour for me to put on my headphones, turn on high concentration mode and roll up my sleeves to get to the main thing: Building new APIs and optimizing the database.

Afternoon

Exchange during the working process of a Backend

  • 1:30 PM – Code Review:It's time to "find the worm" on your colleague's code. At SoftBuild, our culture isBe straightforward but respectful. Comment directly on the code, absolutely no personal attacks. Thanks to these strict "tampering" screens, the source code of the entire system is always clean, optimized and minimizes security holes.
  • 3:00 PM – Cross coordination:Enter into "fiery" (but extremely noisy) meetings with the Frontend team and Product Manager. The goal is to finalize the "data contract" - what the Frontend needs to display, what logic the PM wants, and how the Backend must process and return the data to match.

End of the day

4:30 PM – Push code to Production:The moment of “truth”. Pushing code from the test environment to the live environment is always a mixture of thrill and pride. Seeing the lines of code I cherished officially "live" and serve thousands of users looking for living space on SoftBuild, it feels really "yes".

Real story:Close to the launch of the project filtering feature, the data download speed suddenly slowed down dramatically. Keeping calm and checking the system, I discovered that the database lacked index settings (like a thick book that forgot to make a table of contents). It only took 5 additional minutes, the speed increased 10 times, ensuring everything aired smoothly. Working as a Backend, agility and the ability to withstand pressure are survival skills!

More than lines of code

Looking back, being a Backend is not about "talking" to inanimate machines, but about solving the problem of human experience. Watching the SoftBuild system operate smoothly, helping thousands of people find a satisfactory living space every day is our greatest pride.

For young people who are passionate about programming, my advice is: Be curious and dig deep into nature. Understanding "why the system works" will help you go much further than just typing in superficial code for the sake of it.

What part of Backend work do you find most interesting? If you have any questions about the learning path or necessary skills, just leave a comment below. Bao will answer directly!

Let's start your Backend career

A busy but extremely proud working day for a Backend Engineer at SoftBuild. Feeling that the "backbone" system I designed operates smoothly, processes tens of thousands of data streams without any delay, helps accurately solve the performance problem and brings a seamless housing search experience to users is an achievement that cannot be exchanged.

The story of Master Nguyen Huynh Gia Bao is clear proof: Making a Backend is not dry with just lines of code hidden behind the server. It is the art of combining sharp logical thinking, the ability to withstand high pressure and a deep understanding of real business problems.

Are you ready to step out of your comfort zone, create international standard core systems, handle huge loads and build a solid career path like Gia Bao? Join the SoftBuild team today!

Backend Engineer FAQ

What programming languages and technology tools are the Backend team at SoftBuild using as the main ones?

At SoftBuild, we prioritize system stability, security, and scalability as the number of users increases. Depending on the requirements of each subsystem, engineers often use powerful data processing languages such as Java,Pythonor Node.js.

Regarding the database management system, we flexibly combine SQL and NoSQL solutions, accompanied by cloud computing services (Cloud) to optimize transmission performance.

When there is a disagreement about data design between Backend, Frontend and Product Manager, how will the team resolve it?

Every decision at SoftBuild is centered on real-world data and end-user experience. When there are disagreements in cross-sectional meetings, the parties will analyze the pros and cons of each option based on two criteria: system response speed and feature completion time.

Sometimes, we will build a small test to evaluate feasibility before finalizing the final solution.

The pressure to ensure timely feature launches and the need to write optimal code often go against each other. How does a Backend engineer balance this?

The solution lies in maintaining discipline in the software development process. Breaking up the daily workload into Daily Stand-up sessions helps us control progress.

At the same time, the mandatory Code Review step (cross-checking the source code) in the afternoon helps detect sub-optimal code early. This approach ensures the feature is released on time without leaving long-term risks to the system.

Does a Backend Engineer's work really end after working hours or after pushing code to the live environment?

SoftBuild's system serves customers searching for real estate 24/7. Although we have set up automatic monitoring and warning systems, in the event of a serious incident occurring outside of business hours, Backend engineers will be assigned to be on duty on the system. The team is always ready to check and handle emergency errors to ensure continuous operation of the platform.

For a young programmer who wants to join the Backend team at SoftBuild, what evaluation criteria are the most important?

In addition to solid foundational knowledge of algorithms and databases, SoftBuild especially emphasizes problem-solving skills and initiative in work. We look for candidates who not only know how to write code according to existing requirements, but also know how to ask questions to clearly understand the purpose of the feature and proactively propose more optimal technical solutions.

Today's software development teams face greater pressure than ever: shortened deployment times, ever-increasing security requirements, and rapidly changing AI technology lifecycles. Therefore, many businesses are looking to software consulting companies to shape strategies and deploy actual systems effectively. The global IT services market has reached a size of 1.34 trillion USD by 2024, showing that the demand for reputable implementation partners is still growing strongly across many sectors.

AI is also raising standards across the industry. Gartner predicts global GenAI spending will reach $644 billion by 2025, forcing leaders to no longer accept “flashy” promises but need practical and deployable AI roadmaps. At the same time, IDC predicts that digital transformation spending worldwide could reach nearly $4 trillion by 2027, continuing to drive business modernization programs.

The pace of adoption is also accelerating. According to a McKinsey survey, 65% of organizations said they used generative AI on a regular basis. This makes businesses looking for consultants not only pay attention to technology but also place higher demands on governance, data readiness and change management.

This article will help you clearly understand the role of thesoftware consulting company, selection criteria, as well as suggestions for suitable units for each common business need.

What is Software Consulting Companies?

Thesoftware consulting companyhelps businesses make the right technology decisions and deploy them faster in practice. They participate in the entire value chain, from strategy formulation, system architecture design, product development to operations. At the same time, they help minimize risk through implementation experience, a team of experienced experts, and proven processes.

Typically, a software consulting company will start by clarifying the business goals of the enterprise. Next, they evaluate current systems, data, and team capabilities. Based on that, they proposed an implementation roadmap with trade-offs. Then, they can directly design and develop solutions or accompany internal teams to deploy.

Most consulting units provide services in many aspects. They provide support from product discovery, user experience (UX) design, to cloud architecture and platform building. In addition, they also help modernize legacy systems, optimize data, enhance security, improve software quality and increase release speed. Many companies also provide DevOps services and system operations after deployment.

In terms of terminology, "software consultancy" usually refers to consulting services combined with actual implementation. “Software consulting firms” can include global strategy consulting firms and systems integrators. Meanwhile, “software development consulting firms” are often more technical and product development oriented. In fact, the best partners are those that can flexibly combine all three elements depending on project needs.

  • Providing flexible cooperation models, from strategic consulting to full package implementation.
  • Clear communication, complete documentation and measurable results.

  • The NineHertz

Compare Software Consulting and Software Outsourcing

Software consulting starts with decision making. Consulting units will help businesses clarify goals, constraints and trade-offs. From there, they build an implementation roadmap to minimize risks, while aligning stakeholders on budget, timeline and product direction.

Meanwhile, software outsourcing focuses more on execution capacity. Outsourcing providers will provide a developer team or team to deploy according to predetermined requirements. This model is suitable when the project scope is clear and the business has mastered the product direction.

Nowadays, many companies combine both models. However, the core difference lies in who makes the important decisions. A true software consulting unit will proactively criticize assumptions, analyze risks and propose many optimal solutions. In contrast, a pure outsourcing provider will usually stick to the requirements and focus on providing resources for implementation.

Businesses should choose the consulting model when the problem is unclear and needs to shape the system architecture or technology strategy. On the contrary, outsourcing is a suitable choice when you have a specific plan and only need to expand implementation resources. In practice, these two models can be combined: starting with a short consulting period to determine direction, then moving to the delivery team for stable implementation.

Software consulting firms help businesses “clarify complexity” and speed up the implementation of difficult systems. The best partners are those with both consulting capacity and the technical depth to turn strategies into actual products. Businesses should shortlist partners based on selection criteria and specific needs, then verify through a small pilot and clear evaluation indicators before expanding cooperation.

Choosing the right software consulting company in 2026 actually revolves around one core factor: finding a partner capable of turning strategy into actual operating products without slowing down the pace of business development. When Gartner forecasts total global IT spending may reach6.08 trillion USD by 2026, competitive pressure will become increasingly greater, especially with teams that deploy slowly.

FAQ

How to choose the right software consulting company?

You should evaluate based on their consulting capacity (strategy), implementation ability (delivery), industry experience and how they handle risks. Also, check case studies, real customers and start with a small pilot project to confirm the fit.

When should you choose software consulting instead of outsourcing?

Choose consulting when you are unclear about your requirements, need architectural orientation or technology strategy. Choose outsourcing when you have a clear scope and just need more resources to deploy.

Is the cost of hiring a software consulting company high?

The cost is often higher than pure outsourcing, but in return you receive the right direction from the beginning, reduce risks and save long-term costs by avoiding mistakes in architecture and implementation.

How long does it take to start a consulting project?

Normally, the discovery phase can last from 2–6 weeks depending on complexity. Then, businesses can move into the design and development phase with a clear roadmap.

Is it possible to combine consulting and development?

Yes. Many businesses start with consulting to determine strategy, then turn to the delivery team to implement. This is a popular model that helps optimize both speed and quality.

How to ensure project success when working with partners?

It is necessary to clearly establish KPIs, timelines, scope and communication mechanisms from the beginning. In addition, dividing the project into sprints and periodically checking will help reduce risks and ensure progress.
